messages.subject: R Help and @internal items
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Looking at the StatET R documentation of devtools for instance, I was
surprised to see documentation for non-exported functions, as
load_imports.
Looking at the source code:

#' Load all of the imports for a package
#'
#' The imported objects are copied to the imports environment, and are not
#' visible from R_GlobalEnv. This will automatically load (but not attach)
#' the dependency packages.
#'
#' @keywords internal
load_imports <- function(pkg = ".") {

And the pdf reference manual:
http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/devtools/devtools.pdf do not
include this function.
Is there a way to configure StatET Help to filter these internal items ?

Thanks,

Karl

They should be available in the online help in a regular R console as 
well.  If documentation exists, R will make it available.

THings in pkg-internal.Rd will, I believe, not be included in the 
package pdf, but will be included in the online docs.  If the package 
author doesn't want you to find them, they shouldn't export them in the 
NAMESPACE and document them.

messages.subject: Re: Disable debug mode when using debug()
messages.subject_clean: Disable debug mode when using debug()
messages.body_plain:
On the third tab of the R run configuration dialog box (i.e., R console), there's a checkbox in the "Eclipse integration" section located in the bottom 1/3 of the panel where it says Enable extensions by StatET for improved debug support of R code. If this checkbox is not selected, the function will debug in the main window.

Jim

messages.subject: Update from 3.2 to 3.3 Keybindings
messages.body_plain:
Dear StatET Users and Developers,

I upgraded StatET from 3.2 to 3.3 by adding the new update site. Now I
noticed that 'eval function at point' (mapped to Ctrl+R, Ctrl+F) did
not work anymore. I investigated in the Preferences > General > Keys
menu and found that this shortcut is duplicated there. The first one
is most likely a leftover of the StatET 3.2 package. It does work if I
specify the mentioned keybinding for the second item *only* which
seemingly corresponds to the StatET 3.3 package.

Was there something wrong with my update procedure? Could this be a bug?

Best Regards,
Michael

messages.subject: Re: Update from 3.2 to 3.3 Keybindings
messages.body_plain:
Hi Michael,

Michael Bach wrote [2013-06-10 12:00]:
> Dear StatET Users and Developers,
>
> I upgraded StatET from 3.2 to 3.3 by adding the new update site. Now I
> noticed that 'eval function at point' (mapped to Ctrl+R, Ctrl+F) did
> not work anymore. I investigated in the Preferences > General > Keys
> menu and found that this shortcut is duplicated there. The first one
> is most likely a leftover of the StatET 3.2 package. It does work if I
> specify the mentioned keybinding for the second item *only* which
> seemingly corresponds to the StatET 3.3 package.
>
> Was there something wrong with my update procedure? Could this be a bug?

This is an configuration bug in Eclipse 4, it does not disable commands 
which no longer exists. The problem was already discussed on this 
mailing list, but the thread is missing in the archive. The proposed 
workaround was to reset the keybinding, see also the very last post at:
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/9113321/restoring-default-keybindings-in-eclipse
(-> remove <workspace>/.metadata/.plugins/org.eclipse.e4.workbench)

Regards,
Stephan


>
> Best Regards,
> Michael

messages.subject: StatET format roxygen comments
messages.body_plain:
Dear StatET Users and Developers,

another feature request for an enhanced formatter in the fashion of
Java > Code Style > Formatter. One example where this would be handy
is for auto-filling roxygen comment blocks to a specified line width -
in general to have the Ctrl+Alt+F comparable to PyDev and Java
editors.

Currently, I use a workaround with ESS inside emacs to do the filling.

I am aware of the fact that this is not trivial to implement, but I
think this would help many other users. Feel free to discuss.

Best Regards,
Michael Bach

messages.subject: Remote Console Server: Changed behaviour of RMI registry in new Java versions
messages.subject_clean: Remote Console Server: Changed behaviour of RMI registry in new Java versions
messages.body_plain:
Dear users of the remote server,

please note that Oracle changed the behaviour of the RMI registry in 
Java 7 Update 21, Java 6 Update 45 and Java 5 Update 45 [1] (again [2]).

The solution recommend by Oracle is to specify the codebase at the start 
of the registry. That means for the console server to start the registry 
using:

rmiregistry 
-J-Djava.rmi.server.codebase=file:///<path-to-file-de.walware.rj.server.jar>/

The old workaround [2] still works, if you use it you don't have to 
change anything. It is also possible to disable the new behaviour, but 
not recommend [1].

Regards,
Stephan


[1] 
http://docs.oracle.com/javase/7/docs/technotes/guides/rmi/enhancements-7.html
[2] 
http://lists.r-forge.r-project.org/pipermail/statet-user/2012-January/001201.html


--

messages.subject: StatET not setting memory.limits correctly
messages.body_plain:
I don't recall this being an issue previously, but if I launch R 3.0.1
x64 from within Stat-ET using Eclipse 4.2.2 on Windows:

> memory.limit()
[1] 2047

The same R launched from the GUI:
> memory.limit()
[1] 49139

Now, I can manually set this each time, but this causes issues with a
lot of my code (especially since I run parallel code, and have to
embed the memory.limit call in my worker functions).  I tried setting
R_MAX_MEM_SIZE to 49139 in the Run Configuration Environment tab, but
it seems like it just ignores it.

Any ideas?  As I said, I feel like this is an issue with the latest
version of Stat-et (3.3.0.b201306021645E42sw), as I didn't ever have
the issue previously.

--j
